chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Yasar, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far al-Sakkuni, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sha'iri, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
Whoever defiles the mosque with his phlegm shall meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection smiling, having been given his book in his right hand.

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, the sacred place of worship
key_terms.بِيَمِينِهِ: in his right hand, indicating a favorable outcome
key_terms.ضَاحِكًا: smiling, in a state of joy
key_terms.لَقِيَ اللَّهَ: he met Allah, meaning he came before Allah in the hereafter

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about spitting or leaving phlegm in the mosque and its consequence in the afterlife?
ai.summary: This hadith speaks about conduct related to the mosque and links one's behavior there to the outcome in the hereafter. It presents a consequence on the Day of Resurrection, mentioning being received with joy and being given the record in the right hand.
